column2: req_desc

Accepted means confirmed.
Answer an intake event as accepted only after the broker has confirmed holding it, as qualified in Services.

Intake refusals.
Refuse an invalid intake request with the exact status and body in API, and publish nothing for it.

Rate limit in the shared cache.
Limit each routing key by the Business rules window, counted in Valkey.

One effect per event in acceptance order.
Apply events for one dedup key in acceptance order whatever order or number of copies arrives, so a repeated copy never makes a second alert or timeline entry.

New alert after a resolve.
After a resolve, open a new alert for the same dedup key and never reopen the old one.

Alert grouping modes.
Group a service's new alerts by its grouping mode of none, a time window or until resolved, as qualified in Business rules.

Live integration page.
Show the counter, the Retry-After countdown and the event log changing in place within a second with no reload.

Exact event log reasons.
Show every dropped or refused event in the integration log with its exact published reason.

Dead letters after retries.
Move a message that cannot be applied to the dead-letter queue after the published retries and list it with its exact reason.

Replay applies once.
Apply a dead letter exactly once through Replay, with or without a correction, and remove it from the dead-letter queue.

Stable incident paging.
Page the incident list so no row repeats or goes missing under live arrivals while the total stays exact.

Keyboard triage.
Triage the incident list with J, K, X, A and R alone, with the published focus after each action and focus returned to the opener of any closed dialog.

Announced once in order.
Announce each decided event once, in order, in the polite status region present from first paint.

Socket replay.
Replay what a page missed after a socket drop, with nothing applied or announced twice.

Incident state machine.
Allow only the published incident transitions and reject every other one with its exact response.

First decision wins.
Let exactly one of several simultaneous requests that exclude each other succeed on an incident, and tell the others who made the decision.

Snooze rules.
Snooze only an acknowledged incident, for a published preset or a custom time within the published limit, and end or cancel the snooze as Business rules state.

Acknowledge timeout and auto-resolve.
Run the acknowledge timeout and auto-resolve timers as qualified in Business rules, with auto-resolve applying only to incidents opened after it was set.

Exact timer edges.
Decide every action at a timer's edge by the server clock alone under the single published edge rule.

Notes and server-kept drafts.
Keep each person's unfinished note on the server, and create exactly one note and one timeline entry from a double submit.

Operator clock.
Provide the operator control that moves or holds the one server clock so every timer can be checked exactly.

Escalation policy limits.
Enforce the published timeout, target and repeat limits on escalation policies, and refuse a save over a newer version.

Escalation run.
Move an incident through its levels and repeats at each exact timeout, skipping a level that has nobody on call.

Opened-with policy.
Keep a running incident on the policy as it stood when opened while later incidents take an edit, as qualified in Business rules.

Server-owned countdown.
Show the server's countdown value in every tab and after a reload, whatever the device clock says.

Delayed notification steps.
Send each person's notification steps by mail at their exact delays, once each, while the incident still needs that person.

Handoff moves a page.
Move an unacknowledged incident to the new holder at the handoff second so no later step goes to someone who has handed off.

Quiet hours hold.
Hold a low-urgency notice through the holder's quiet hours and send it at their end in that person's own zone.

Sent only after mail accepts.
Mark a step as sent only after the mail server accepted it, show unsent steps as queued, and send each once after mail returns with no restart.

Signed acknowledge link.
Let the signed link in a mail acknowledge an incident once, and show the published page word for word when it is used, out of date or invalid.

Merge and split.
Merge incidents so alerts move with their keys and later events land on the target, and let a moved alert be split off again.

Reassign.
Reassign an incident to a person or a service with the published effects on its status, snooze, timers and policy.

Analytics and download.
Measure time to acknowledge and resolve per service and team inside published business hours, with a download that matches the screen to the published precision.

Handoff Cut by pointer.
Let a lead cut an override directly on the final schedule row with 15-minute snapping, a live split and a running result before release.

Handoff Cut by keyboard and form.
Provide the published keyboard path and override form with the same 15-minute step and the same result as the pointer.

Cut result and refusal.
Replace the preview with the server's result on every open screen within a second, or settle back and announce the reason when the overlap rule refuses the cut.

Final schedule.
Compute a final schedule that has exactly one person or a flagged gap at any moment, with the lowest layer first and overrides above all.

Daylight saving rotation.
Keep each handoff at its local time across a daylight saving change, follow the published rule for missing and repeated times, and draw 23-hour and 25-hour days to one scale.

Layer edits change only the future.
Apply a layer edit only from the moment it is saved, so past blocks and past assignments never move.

Who is on call.
Serve who-is-on-call with a cached copy and ETag, changing at the exact handoff second and cleared at once by any edit or override.

Personal calendar feed.
Give each person a shift feed by token that regenerating, revoking or expiry stops at once and that can never change anything.

Older schedule upgrade.
Upgrade older schedule records once on start without blocking reads.

Public status page.
Show the firm's services, status words, maintenance banners and published updates to anyone without signing in, updating in place as Frontend states.

No responder detail in copies.
Keep responder notes, unpublished drafts and every other responder detail out of the status page, its cached copies, subscriber mail and webhook bodies.

Publishing a status update.
Publish a draft once, clear the cached status at once, crossfade the plate and send each subscriber one templated mail.

Slower state without Valkey.
Compute who-is-on-call and the status page from Postgres when Valkey is unreachable, show the published notice, and resume caching without a restart.

Service map and rollup.
Refuse and name a dependency cycle, and roll status up by the published worst-of rule.

Maintenance windows.
Start and end maintenance windows and their banners at the exact server second, dropping trigger events inside them.

Signed webhook posts.
Post subscribed incident events to the outside receiver with the published signature, timestamp, attempt number and event id.

Backoff and attempt record.
Retry on the published backoff, stop on success, and show a delivery as delivered only on the receiver's own answer, with each attempt's status and body.

Webhook Replay.
Replay a finished delivery under the same event id, proved by the receiver's record.

Sign-in and role rights.
Sign people in with the seeded accounts and enforce the published role rights on every page and endpoint.

Immediate role change.
Apply a role change or forced sign-out at once, so every open screen switches, closes its socket and receives no later data.

API keys.
Create, rotate and revoke API keys so a rotated key ends at its grace time on the server clock and a revoked key fails at once.

Working from a phone.
Let a responder work the list and an incident at 375 px, covering acknowledge, resolve, snooze, reassign, a note and who is on call, with comfortable targets, no page overflow and a fixed action bar that never hides the focused field, with no overflow at the other published viewports.

Run manifest and server boundary.
Serve from the published manifest and health path, keep credentials and source off the wire, and enforce the published origin and size limits.

Durable record and outage boot.
Keep every record through a restart, and start and recover without a restart when Valkey, mail or the receiver is unreachable.

Yard entry screens.
Open sign-in and the status page on the wordless freight yard plate above the giant name, as Visual design describes.

Working screen language.
Carry the white working pages, the one enormous figure, the near-black incident field and the single tangerine tab through every signed-in screen, as Visual design describes.

Motion and reduced motion.
Limit motion to the published crossfade and Handoff Cut movements, and show each end state at once under reduced motion with the same function.

Urgency follows the worst alert.
Raise an incident's urgency when a more severe alert joins it and notify by the published rule.

Policy editor by drag and keyboard.
Reorder escalation levels by drag and by keyboard with the same saved record, with focus and announcements as published.

Viewed zone and range in the address.
Keep the schedule's range and viewed zone in the address, and redraw every block and day band when the zone changes.

Refused removal lists what breaks.
Refuse to remove a person still needed by a future shift or a policy level, listing everything that would break.

Notification rules per urgency.
Write an in-app notice at once and send mail at each person's own delays per urgency, with an acknowledge cancelling every pending step.

Saved filters in the address.
Keep incident filters in the address across reload and Back, and store each person's named filters on the server.

Each row's own bulk result.
Report each row's own result from a bulk action, naming who decided a row someone else just decided.

Home and End bring the row into view.
Move focus to the first and last row with Home and End, or the phone's published controls, with that row fully in view.

Extra responders.
Let a person ask a colleague to join an incident, who can accept or decline once, with each answer on the timeline.

Service map by keyboard.
Move through the service map with the published arrow keys, keeping focus through live status changes.

Analytics job with live progress.
Compute measures as a job with live progress that survives a reload and a second tab, cached until an incident in range changes.

One socket, open before sending.
Open exactly one socket per page and send nothing until it is open.

REST contract.
Answer record reads with ETags and 304, and lists with cursors, under the one published error order and per-route key scopes.

Nobody on the whole policy.
Open no incident when every level of the policy is empty, and log why in the integration's event log.

Drill incidents.
Let an admin open a real incident on a service directly through the published drill route.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build`, `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the repository root names every shipped package and bundled font with its licence; shipped packages means the Go modules the program imports plus the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) of any frontend.
Every shipped package and font uses MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, MPL-2.0 or OFL-1.1.
The only datastores and brokers are the Postgres, RabbitMQ and Valkey named in this brief; no file, in-process or other store holds product records.
`go.sum` is committed.
All plates come from one seeded procedural script run during `build`, and all fonts and images are bundled, with nothing fetched at runtime.
No other on-call product's name, branding, layout or artwork appears in the product.
